notes:
Copilot's in-REPL reset ROTATES the session id: /clear and /new both call clearHistory, which creates a new session and switches to it (CLI 1.0.77 bundle, app.js @8632467). The recipe sends /clear, because only /clear (abandon:true) also closes and evicts the outgoing session — /new may keep it alive as a background session. Shape: the v1 birth is the two-phase presession model the copilot column uses (proc-<PID> row first, then the real <session-id> once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt); v2_session_birth carries new_session:true so it can match NEITHER the proc- row NOR the first real session; old_session_ended asserts transcript_removed for the FIRST real session and is anchored to v2_session_birth (not to the reset) because PIDManager's same-PID cleanup fires at the NEW session's pid_discovered, i.e. after B is already visible. v2_session_birth's 90 s window is deliberately wide: the post-reset directory mints nothing until the next prompt writes events.jsonl into it (sessionIDFromPath accepts only that constant filename). PROVISIONAL on one point — whether the daemon first observes the post-reset session in ready or straight into working is a race unsettleable from source, since events.jsonl already holds session.start … user.message when it first appears; if record finds it born working, drop v2_session_birth and move new_session:true onto v2_turn_start, leaving every other phase unchanged. model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only auto and the router picks gpt-5-mini or claude-haiku-4.5 per turn.

RECORDED 2026-08-05 (CLI 1.0.78). `/clear` DOES rotate the session id — settled from a recording rather than from the bundle: two session-state directories are minted, the pre-reset session runs its turn (6d5d9186: working 19:00:33.041 → ready 19:00:39.863), `/clear` mints 469f078a which runs its own turn (working 19:00:50.172 → ready 19:00:52.824), and the old row is swept at 19:00:52.883.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED, TWICE: BOTH real sessions are born directly into `working` (commit 3cde4f8d) — copilot writes events.jsonl only when a prompt is sent, so at discovery each file already holds its open turn. session_birth/v1_turn_start and v2_session_birth/v2_turn_start are therefore each ONE phase, and the rotation is proved by v2_turn_start carrying new_session against a session id matching neither the pre-reset one nor the proc-<PID> placeholder.

DRIVER FIX THIS CELL FORCED: the first attempt curated only the POST-reset session. The staging contract is built from the per-slot SES_TRANSCRIPT array and a reset reuses its slot, so clearing it in place left session.uuids with one line, run-cell.sh exported no IRRLICHT_EXTRA_SESSION_IDS, and half the arc was dropped — even though the raw daemon recording held it correctly. The driver now parks the outgoing transcript in RETIRED_TRANSCRIPTS and appends it to the contract, and the run reports `multi-session: primary=469f078a…, extras=6d5d9186…`.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
The first prompt materializes events.jsonl, so the first real <session-id> session reconciles under a different id and is born DIRECTLY into working (commit 3cde4f8d)
assistant.turn_end settles the first turn back to ready on the PRE-reset session

THE ROTATION: after /clear, a session id matching neither the pre-reset session nor the proc-<PID> placeholder appears and runs the next prompt. It is born straight into working for the same reason the first one was — its events.jsonl exists only because a prompt was sent into it. `/clear` mints a new session rather than truncating the old one in place
The second turn completes back to ready on the NEW session; final state ready, and the session never entered waiting
Spec: 'Old session disappears' — the pre-reset row is swept once the rotation is observed, so the dashboard shows one live copilot session rather than an abandoned pair
